newsitem.title: USA: Federated, Dayton Hudson report latest results.
newsitem.headline: Federated, Dayton Hudson report latest results.

text.p: Federated Department Stores Inc., owner of the Bloomingdale's and R.H. Macy & Co. department store chains, Tuesday reported an 18 percent gain in net profits for its latest quarter despite a slight dip in sales.

At the same time, rival Dayton Hudson Corp. said operating profits in its department store division fell during its fourth quarter and fiscal 1996, but its Target and Mervyn's sectors posted increases.

Federated said it earned $289 million, or $1.39 per share, in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Feb. 1, compared with profits of $245 million, or $1.21 per share, in the year-ago period. Net sales in the latest quarter were $5.03 billion, down 4.4 percent from $5.26 billion a year earlier.
For the year, Cincinnati-based Federated's net income was $265.9 million, or $1.28 a share, compared with profits of $74.6 million, or 39 cents a share, for the 53 weeks ended Feb. 3, 1996.
Sales for the year totalled $15.2 billion, an increase of 1.2 percent over the $15 billion during the 53-week 1995 fiscal year.
During the second half of 1995, Federated operated 26 Broadway stores that subsequently were sold or closed.

"Federated's primary objective for 1997 is to focus on the aggressive execution of our current strategies, with the goal of producing (comparable)-store sales growth and further improving our earnings performance," said Allen Questrom, chairman and chief executive officer.

Federated currently operates more than 400 department stores and 150 speciality stores in 36 states. Its department stores operate under the names of Bloomingdale's, The Bon Marche, Burdines, Goldsmith's, Lazarus, Macy's, Rich's and Stern's.

Minneapolis-based Dayton Hudson said its operating earnings for the fourth quarter ended Feb. 1 were $296 million, or $1.27 a share, compared with $228 million, or 98 cents a share, a year ago. The earnings per share were just above analysts' estimates of $1.25 a share, according to First Call, which tracks Wall Street estimates.
Revenues rose to $8.16 billion from $7.95 billion.
For the full year, operating earnings were $555 million, or $2.35 a share, vs. $311 million, or $1.30 a share. Revenues rose to $25.37 billion from $23.52 billion.

The fourth-quarter and full-year results included a previously announced real-estate-related, pre-tax charge of $134 million, or 35 cents per share. The results also included extraordinary after-tax charges for debt redemption of $1 million, or 1 cent per share, for the quarter, and $11 million, or 5 cents per share, for the year.

The retailer, which operates 1,100 stores in 38 states, said it was optimistic about its 1997 performance. It said it had reduced its retail debt as a percent of total capital to 50 percent, the middle of its target range. The company also said it was able to reduce its debt during the year while funding $1.3 billion in capital expenditures.
Dayton Hudson said operating profit at its Target stores rose 45 percent for the year to $1.042 billion from $719 million in fiscal 1995.
"Target had a great year," said Dean Ramos, an analyst at investment banker Dain Bosworth. "They're a very well run company," he said. "Within the discount store business, Target is one of best."
Operating profit before charges at Mervyn's rose to $267 million, compared with $100 million the previous year.
At Dayton Hudson's department stores, operating profit for the year fell to $128 million before charges, compared with $184 million in fiscal 1995.
Dayton Hudson's stock was off $1 at $41 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange, while Federated was up 62.5 cents at $35.75, also on the NYSE.
